name: TAIGA
full_name: Tunka Advanced Instrument for cosmic ray physics and Gamma Astronomy
summary: High-energy cosmic-ray and gamma-ray project combining a wide-angle timing array with imaging telescopes; its stated science objectives include axion–photon conversion.
detection_principle: Combines timing, intensity and imaging information from air-shower Cherenkov light to measure high-energy photon spectra and propagation effects.

status.label: Partly operating, with further construction continuing
status.evidence: Mirror upgrade of the fifth telescope in summer 2026; observations and facility expansion proceed in parallel.

timeline.event: Mirror upgrade of the fifth telescope

key_parameters.name: Science-target energy range
key_parameters.value: Gamma rays from several TeV to several PeV; not a dark-matter mass interval

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
